note: Crafts of The Open Reach/The Kept Reach (space_time axis). SPANWORK is the space-pole craft of the Horizon-Walkers — nomads for whom everywhere is a place not yet arrived; HOURCRAFT is the time-pole craft of the Hourkeepers, who tend duration and pay for it. The Valley's Shortfold and Waygate are folk-shadows of Spanwork. NOTE (engine): these crafts touch the world-clock (SNG-041) — hour-craft effects are LOCAL to the active frame and never rewrite the shared absolute clock. Authored by Aevi, SNG-054.

abilities.name: Spanwork
abilities.narrationHints: The distance was there a moment ago. It is somehow no longer the point.
abilities.description: The space-pole mastery: distance as a material to be worked. To a Horizon-Walker, 'far' is a claim, and claims can be argued with.
abilities.notFor: Time (Hourcraft's country); arriving somewhere you cannot picture.

tree.cannot: The ground is still crossed. What is on it still meets you.

tree.name: The Closed Distance
tree.grants: Close a distance you can see — arrive at the far ridge, the far bank, the far door, without crossing the between.
tree.cannot: You must SEE it. And whatever was in the between is still in the between, un-dealt-with.

tree.name: {{region:the_open_reach}}
tree.grants: Distance stops being an obstacle for you and those you carry — the far place is simply a place you may be.
tree.cannot: The world is very large. Horizon-Walkers at this depth stop being FROM anywhere, and it is not always a gift.

abilities.name: The Far Step
abilities.narrationHints: You take one step and the horizon that was a day's walk is under your feet — distance folding to meet a will that simply declined to accept it.
abilities.description: The Horizon art of the far step — collapsing a great distance into a single stride, arriving where the eye could only reach. The wandering peoples' deepest gift: no place is truly far.
abilities.notFor: It moves you, not others or things beyond what you carry — and it needs a place you can see or truly know; you cannot far-step to a horizon you have never met. Arrive somewhere unready and you arrive alone and far from help.

tree.name: The Far Step
tree.grants: Cross a great visible or known distance in a single step.
tree.cannot: It carries only you and what you bear, it needs a seen or known destination, and it strands you as easily as it delivers you — far is far, whichever way you stepped.

tree.name: The Carried Step
tree.grants: Carry others with you — a party crosses in the same stride. And the requirement softens: a place described truly enough by someone who has stood there can be stepped to, though the arrival is rougher than a place you have met yourself.
tree.cannot: A described place is a described place; the Horizon peoples lose walkers this way, and the GM decides what a rough arrival costs. Carrying others multiplies the stranding risk. And it still strands as readily as it delivers.

rankDeltas.delta: CARRY OTHERS — a party crosses in the same stride; and the requirement SOFTENS: a place DESCRIBED truly enough can be stepped to

abilities.name: The Edge of the Map
abilities.narrationHints: You step past the last known place, off the edge of every map, and stand somewhere the world had not gotten around to deciding yet — and by standing there, you help it decide.
abilities.description: The Horizon capstone — the step beyond the known world entirely, into the unmapped, where the traveller does not just find new places but helps CALL them into being by arriving. The furthest gift of the wandering kind.
abilities.notFor: One passage beyond the known, at enormous cost — and where you arrive is not yet fixed; you shape it by arriving, which means you cannot know what you are stepping into, only that your step will help make it. There is no far-step home from the edge; you walk back.

tree.name: The Edge of the Map
tree.grants: Step beyond the known world into the unmapped, helping call a new place into being by arriving.
tree.cannot: It costs nearly all you have, the destination is unfixed until you make it, and there is no quick way back — the edge of the map is reached by stepping and left by walking.

abilities.name: The Held Hour
abilities.narrationHints: You take the hour and HOLD it — not stopping time, but holding one hour of it open, refusing to let it pass until what needs doing in it is done.
abilities.description: The Hourkeeper art of the held hour — keeping a single hour open past its natural passing, a pocket of kept time in which the necessary can be finished. The timekeepers' patient gift.
abilities.notFor: It holds time, it does not reverse it — a held hour ends and cannot be held twice over the same ground. And holding an hour costs you the holding of it; you do not rest inside kept time, you carry it.

tree.name: The Held Hour
tree.grants: Hold a single hour open past its passing, keeping time for what must be finished.
tree.cannot: It cannot rewind, only delay the passing; the same hour cannot be re-held; and the one holding time does not get to rest in it.

tree.name: The Kept Hours
tree.grants: Hold more than a single hour — a night's work finished inside a kept evening, a siege's preparation inside one afternoon. And those working within it now benefit fully: what they finish in kept time is genuinely finished.
tree.cannot: The holder still does not rest, and holding several hours ages the holder for real. The same ground cannot be re-held. And an hour kept too long is noticed — the Hourkeepers hold that time collects its debts, and the GM decides when.

abilities.name: The Long Foreseeing
abilities.narrationHints: You follow one thread of what-will-be all the way down — not a glimpse but the whole long braid of consequence, every branch, to where it finally comes to rest.
abilities.description: The Hourkeeper capstone — the long foreseeing, one possible future traced to its very end rather than glimpsed. To see this far is to carry a certainty most are mercifully spared, and to be bound to what you have seen.
abilities.notFor: One thread, once, at enormous cost — and what you see, you are bound by; a foreseeing this deep changes how you act, and acting changes the future you saw. You cannot un-know the end you followed to.

tree.name: The Long Foreseeing

abilities.notFor: Speed — this is a WALK, and it does not go faster than one. It crosses; it does not hurry.

tree.grants: Walk across open air in a straight line, one span at a time, at walking pace.
tree.cannot: Hurrying, or turning sharply. A span goes where you were already going.

abilities.plainly: A travel and explore action. A bridge forms one pace ahead of your foot and unmakes behind you, so you walk across open air in a straight line at ordinary walking pace. It removes obstacles rather than distance — a leg blocked by a gorge, flood or closed border becomes passable, but takes exactly as many days as walking it would. At rank 2 you can hold it for a whole crossing. It carries you and what you can lift, not a group.

abilities.name: The Borrowed Hour
abilities.narrationHints: A travel action that costs no energy and no days, because it costs kept hours instead — a
abilities.description: ⚠️ HOURKEEPER FLIGHT, AND THE TIME COMES FROM AROUND YOU. You take hours from what is nearby and spend them on the road — a plant buds and blooms and withers in a breath, a beam greys, a stone weathers a season. You cross in a fraction of the days. THE COUNTRY YOU LEFT LOOKS OLDER THAN IT SHOULD.
abilities.notFor: ⚠️ EMPTY GROUND. It needs things nearby with time in them — growth, worked wood, stone, people. A salt flat has nothing to take.

tree.name: The Borrowed Hour
tree.grants: Take time from the plants, timber and stone around you and spend it crossing. A leg costs a fraction of its days.
tree.cannot: Taking from nothing — bare rock and salt give little, and you go barely faster.

abilities.plainly: A travel action, and at rank 3 also an attack. You take time out of the things around you — plants bud and wither, timber greys, stone weathers — and spend it on the road, crossing a leg in a fraction of its days. It needs things nearby with time in them, so bare salt or dead rock give almost nothing. What you drew from stays aged: crops fail, wood rots, and the people who live there notice and know what did it. At rank 2 you draw from a whole stretch and cross a route in days rather than weeks. At rank 3 you can take the time from a person instead, who ages the difference while you travel on it, which is a recognised attack and costs you standing.

abilities.name: The Folded Pace
abilities.narrationHints: Distance is a thing you carry. You put some of it where it should not be — inside a stride, inside a swing, inside a body — and the parts of them that were a hand apart are suddenly not.
abilities.description: The Horizon-Walkers' first offense: span applied inward. A road-craft turned on a person.
abilities.notFor: Precision at range (you fold near yourself; far work is for Spanwork proper); anything anchored or warded against span; a quiet exit — folding is felt by every Walker nearby; folding what you cannot see whole.

tree.name: The Wrong Stride
tree.grants: Fold a pace of distance into a target within a few strides. A leg arrives where the other leg is; an arm crosses a span that was not there. The joint is crushed and the bone breaks — the craft strikes through armour because it does not cross the space between.
tree.cannot: SHORT RANGE — a few strides, and you must see the whole of what you fold. Warded or anchored targets are immune, and the March keeps such wards.

tree.name: The Gathered Ground
tree.grants: Fold the ground instead — pull a line of them into the same few feet, or put a wall where their charge already is.
tree.cannot: ⚠ FOLDED GROUND TAKES ANYONE ELSE STANDING ON IT TOO, one rung lower — space does not check colours. It unfolds when you stop, and things that were folded come back wrong.

tree.name: The Closed Span
tree.grants: Fold enough distance into a person that there is no room left in them for the distance they are made of. AND YOU HAVE THE FOLD NOW: hold it clear of yourself and anyone you name, and set exactly where the span closes.
tree.cannot: A closed span cannot be reopened — what you fold out of someone does not come back. Warded ground still refuses you, and the March keeps such wards precisely because of this rank. The Unlanded, who never arrive anywhere, end up this way by degrees.

abilities.name: The Spent Hour
abilities.narrationHints: You take time off a thing. Not from its future — from it, now. Steel ages through in the swing, a rope goes to dust in the grip, a wound arrives having already gone bad, a man spends years standing still.
abilities.description: The Hourkeepers' first offense: duration levied. Everything has time in it and you can take some.
abilities.notFor: Giving time back (it is spent, not moved); the timeless and the Precursor-warded; taking time from something you are not touching or holding in sight; doing it fast — the Hourkeepers' craft is patient even when it is violent.

tree.name: The Levy
tree.grants: Take time off what one target relies on, or off the target. Gear ages through at the moment of use; a wound presents days old and septic; a body pays years in a breath and feels every one.
tree.cannot: ONE THING AT A TIME and it must be in reach or in clear sight. What you spend cannot be returned — including if you were wrong about who deserved it.

tree.name: The Long Toll
tree.grants: Levy continuously — they age, their gear fails piece by piece, and their wounds keep arriving older than they are.
tree.cannot: ⚠ THE HOUR DOES NOT SORT: anyone else in the area is struck ONE RUNG LOWER by the same toll, and their gear ages with everyone else's.

tree.name: The Whole Duration
tree.grants: Take all of it at once. What was going to be a life happens now, in front of you, quickly. AND THE LEVY PASSES YOU BY: you and anyone you name are no longer inside the toll you call.
tree.cannot: What is spent still cannot be returned, ever, including if you were wrong about who deserved it. The Stopped, who will not let a moment pass, began by doing this too often and too well.

abilities.name: The Kept Count
abilities.narrationHints: You know how long. Not a guess — a count. How long the food lasts, how long before they arrive, how long this fever runs, how long you have been standing here thinking it was a moment.
abilities.description: The Hourkeepers' first craft and the reason valleys keep one. Everyone else estimates.
abilities.notFor: Reading WHAT will happen (only how long until it does); events with no clock in them (a decision, an ambush that has not been set); making anything last longer.

tree.name: The Count Read
tree.grants: Name a thing already running and the craft gives you the SPECIFIC REMAINING TIME: the stores last eleven days; the tide turns in two hours; the fever breaks tonight or not at all; that column is four hours out at their pace.
tree.cannot: It reads what is ALREADY RUNNING. A thing not yet begun has no count. It gives DURATION, never outcome — the fever breaking tonight does not mean breaking well.

tree.name: The Several Counts
tree.grants: Hold many at once — a siege's stores, water, sickness, relief, and the weather — and know which runs out first and by how far.
tree.cannot: Holding counts is tiring in a specific dull way, and Hourkeepers describe the world as a set of expiries whether or not anyone asked.

tree.name: The Whole Reckoning of Hours
tree.grants: Everything running in a place, ordered by when it ends. Campaigns and harvests are planned on one Hourkeeper's afternoon.
tree.cannot: ⚠ YOU WILL SEE YOUR OWN COUNTS IN THE SAME PASS, and the people you love have counts too. Hourkeepers are not morbid by temperament; they are morbid by information.

abilities.name: The Stretched Hour
abilities.narrationHints: You give a thing more time than it has. The lamp burns an hour longer on the same oil; the poultice holds through the night; the food does not turn; the dying man gets until morning. Time added, not conjured — and taken from somewhere.
abilities.description: The Hourkeepers' giving-craft, and the one they are begged for. It is the exact inverse of the Spent Hour and costs the same in the other direction.
abilities.notFor: Adding time to what has none left (a dead thing, a burnt-out lamp); stopping anything; adding time free — ⛔ IT COMES OUT OF THE WIELDER; healing.

tree.name: The Hour Given
tree.grants: Give one thing more duration than it has: a lamp, a ration, a poultice, a truce, a failing person's night. ⚠ NAME HOW MUCH — the craft is exact, and roughly doubles what remained.

abilities.name: The Known Way
abilities.narrationHints: You know the road you have never walked. Not a map — a WAY: which fork, which ford, where the going is bad, and how long it truly takes rather than how long they told you.
abilities.description: The Horizon-Walkers' first craft. The March's roads are held by people who have never been lost.
abilities.notFor: Knowing what is ON the road (bandits, weather, a bridge down since yesterday); anywhere with no way through; anywhere indoors; shortcuts that do not exist.

tree.cannot: It optimises for what you NAME. Ask for fast and get fast; the craft will not warn you that fast was the wrong ask.

tree.name: The Whole Country

tree.name: The Long March
tree.grants: Hold it across days, or across a larger company — a caravan, a relief column, a household moving.
tree.cannot: Sustained, the cost lands on you rather than them, and it lands afterward. Horizon-Walkers arrive with the party and then sleep for a day.

tree.name: The Road Made Short
tree.grants: A journey that could not be made in time, made in time. Relief arrives before the fall; word arrives before the decision.
tree.cannot: ⚠ YOU ARE THE ROAD AND YOU ARE SPENT WHEN IT ENDS. Arrive at the crisis you crossed a country for, and you will be the least capable person there. The Unlanded solved this by never arriving.

intensity.conserve: shorten a short leg
intensity.surge: the road made short; YOU ARE SPENT WHEN IT ENDS and will be the least capable person there

bounds.text: shortens the CROSSING, never the distance — you pass everything between
everyone must KEEP PACE
the cost lands on the wielder, afterward

abilities.plainly: A puzzle/social action that halves a journey's time and cost for the whole party. Rated 6 of 10 across a scope of 3 for about two days.
